title: Animal Farm, George Orwell
subject: litterature
description: In 1945, Orwell tells of a farm where the animals chase away the man, then see the pigs regain power. A clear allegory of the Russian Revolution and revolutionary betrayal.

hero.hook: Thirty thousand words, animals, and a political lesson that the world has yet to learn.

blocks.text: Published in **1945**, **Animal Farm** looks like a children's story. Beneath this simple appearance, **George Orwell** describes how a popular revolution can be confiscated by a corrupt elite. In just **30,000 words**, he delivers one of the most effective **[[Allegory of the Russian Revolution]]**s ever written.

blocks.caption: Pigs in power: the fable that denounces revolutionary corruption.

sections.title: A surgical allegory of Soviet history

blocks.text: The book was born during the **[[World War II]]**, when the USSR was the ally of the West against Nazi Germany. Criticizing **Stalin** then seems like a political betrayal. Orwell waits until the end of the conflict to publish. Each animal corresponds to a historical figure: **Old Major** evokes **Marx** and **Lenin**, **Napoleon** tracing **Stalin**, **Snowball** recalls **Trotsky**, rival of Stalin, exiled then assassinated.
T.S. Eliot, then editor, refused the manuscript on the grounds that intelligent pigs might offend statesmen.

Napoleon's **dogs** represent the secret police and political terror. **Malabar**, the hardworking horse, embodies the **[[proletariat]]** exploited to the point of total exhaustion. **Brille-Babil**, the pig propagandist, transforms each failure into an official victory, rewriting history as the days go by. Orwell describes the **[[Stalinism]]** with the precision of a pamphlet and the lightness of a fable.

sections.title: The shift: from utopia to dictatorship

blocks.text: The animals chase the farmer **Jones**, symbol of **[[Tsar Nicholas II]]**, reversed in **1917**. They proclaim **Animalism** and write the **Seven Commandments** on the barn wall. Equality finally seems possible. Then Napoleon chases Snowball with his dogs trained for violence and sets up terror.

blocks.caption: The farm at the start: a utopia which tips towards dictatorship.

blocks.text: The windmill becomes a symbol of forced mobilization: the animals exhaust themselves building it while the pigs declare themselves “intellectual workers” and monopolize the resources. Apples and milk are first reserved for leaders, in the name of the “brain” that needs to be fed. Corruption begins with small privileges and then becomes a norm. The public trials and executions are reminiscent of the great Stalinist purges of the 1930s.

sections.title: The modification of language and the final betrayal

blocks.text: Orwell shows that he who controls words controls perceived reality. The pigs change the Commandments at night, when the animals sleep: “No animal shall sleep in a bed” becomes “with sheets.” The alcohol ban earns the “excessive” rating. The collective memory is erased word by word, until no one remembers the original.
All animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others.

It’s a **[[Newspeak]]** before its time: language no longer communicates, it masks. In the end, the pigs walk on two legs, dress up, and banquet with human farmers. The other animals, looking from pig to man and from man to pig, no longer distinguish one from the other. The **[[Russian Revolution]]** delivered exactly what it claimed to combat.

If the book primarily targets the Russian Revolution, its message goes beyond Soviet history. Orwell analyzes submission, propaganda and the fragility of ideals in the face of personal ambition. Without critical education and without collective memory, people see their dreams of freedom distorted by those who take power in the name of the people.

Sold more than **30 million** copies, the novel touches readers of all ages and all cultures. As a child, we read a story about animals; as an adult, we read a treatise on political science. The lesson remains simple and current: when words lose their meaning, physical freedom quickly follows. Here Orwell prepares the themes that he will push to the extreme in **1984** four years later.
**Animal Farm** shows that a betrayed revolution involves the manipulation of language and the confiscation of memory. Orwell proves that a short fable can say more than a thousand-page speech.
